body:
@powtac at each keystroke we update the url (no matter if we use native browser history or fake one using location.hash).

Then, when using native browser history API, on top of updating the url at each keystroke, we create a new history state after the thresold.

The states we are talking about are the ones used when you hit "back", only. They should represent the times where you stop typing/meaningful queries/half queries.

Here's an example:

* history state is empty query
* t0: type t (url bar has: t, history state is empty query)
* t0+30ms: type e (url bar has: te, history state is empty query)
* t0+600ms: type s (url bar has: tes, history state is empty query)
* t0 + 700ms: type t (url bar has: test, new state is created)
* t0 + 900ms: type e (url bar has: teste, history state is "test")

Then if you stop writing, url bar is "teste", history state should be "teste" (because you stopped typing for more than 500ms more (900 + 500 = 1400 so two times thresold).

Then if you hit "back button", you will go to "test" and if you hit back button again you will go to empty query.

Hope this long explanation is clearer.

I think a lot of people thinks thresold might be a debounce url bar set. It's just the time after we create a new history state entry in the browser.
